questions.prompt: Is triangle ABC similar to triangle DEF? If so, describe a similarity transformation that maps ABC onto DEF; if not, explain.

sections.skill: Prove that all circles are similar

branch.new_demand: Extend the transformation definition of similarity to curved figures (circles).
branch.builds_on: A second extension of MAIN: FORWARD 1 handles turned and flipped triangles; FORWARD 2 applies the definition to circles.

questions.skill: Prove that all circles are similar
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Circle C₁ has center A and radius r; circle C₂ has center B and radius s. Prove that C₁ and C₂ are similar.
questions.prompt_markup: Circle C₁ has center A and radius r; circle C₂ has center B and radius s. Prove that C₁ and C₂ are similar.
questions.correct_answer: A translation and a dilation map C₁ onto C₂.
questions.required_method: Translate A to B, then dilate about B with scale factor s/r; show the image of C₁ is C₂.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: the translation maps C₁ to the circle with center B and radius r; the dilation about B with factor s/r sends each point at distance r from B to a point at distance s, so the image is C₂ (and every point of C₂ is reached).
